title: Anchor for an unpinned field of oscillator cells: lowest eigenvector, long-range mark and weighing

key_results.statement: In the limit $M\to\infty$ (min-max convergence of the compressions) a lowest eigenvector of the block exists iff $A>0$; otherwise the lowest eigenvalue of $C_M$ tends to $-\infty$ or to the bottom of a continuum.

Without an anchor a lowest eigenvector exists iff $\mathcal L_n+\mathcal A>0$ (reduced Laplacian of the body places plus ${\rm diag}(2\mu_iF_2^{(i)})$); necessary $\sum_i\mu_iF_2^{(i)}>0$; without bodies with $F_2\ne0$ there is none, the field alone has none, and the whole contract (all blocks) has none for any bodies of (G2).
Without an anchor, one body with $F_2\ne0$: a lowest eigenvector exists iff $\sigma={\rm sign}\,F_2$, for every level; otherwise the lowest eigenvalue tends to $-\infty$.
Without an anchor, two bodies: a lowest eigenvector exists iff $\alpha_1+\alpha_2>0$ and $\alpha_1\alpha_2+(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)/r_{12}>0$, $\alpha_i=2\mu_iF_2^{(i)}$, $r_{12}$ the resistance distance.
A body with $\mu F_2>0$ acts as an anchor of strength $2\mu F_2$ at its own place, but alone its $g_s$-linear cost is $-F_1g_s/(2F_2)$ at every place (no weight) and its cost has no expansion in $s$.

Anchored Green function $G_a(x,y)=1/\kappa_a+\frac12[r(x,h)+r(y,h)-r(x,y)]$, $r(x,y)=2[g(0)-g(x-y)]$, exact for every $L$ on ring and cubic torus; $G_a(h,\cdot)=1/\kappa_a$; ring $r=s(L-s)/(\kappa_hL)$.

Resolvent of the anchored field by Sherman–Morrison: $R_{xy}(
u)=\gamma_

u(0))$.

With the anchor a lowest eigenvector exists iff $\Gamma_n^{-1}+\mathcal A>0$; one body iff $1+2\mu F_2\Gamma(x)>0$, $\Gamma(x)=1/\kappa_a+r(x,h)$; always for $\mu F_2\ge0$; for $\mu F_2<0$ it fails on the ring beyond a finite distance, and on the cubic torus ($L\to\infty$) holds at every place iff $2M_k|F_2|\Gamma_\infty\le1$.

With the anchor, two bodies: a lowest eigenvector exists iff $(1+\alpha_1\Gamma(x_1))(1+\alpha_2\Gamma(x_2))>\alpha_1\alpha_2G_{12}^2$ and $\Gamma(x_1)+\Gamma(x_2)+(\alpha_1+\alpha_2)(\Gamma(x_1)\Gamma(x_2)-G_{12}^2)>0$; sufficient $\bar a(\max_i\Gamma(x_i)+G_{12})<1$; two bodies that each meet the one-body condition need not meet it.

Made field $\phi_a(x)=-g_sG_a(x,x_s)$: a uniform shift plus a place-dependent part; on the cubic torus ($L\to\infty$) source plus opposite image at the anchor over a nonzero constant; on the line $-g_s[1/\kappa_a+\min(d_x,d_s)/\kappa_h]$ on one side of $h$.

Field constants $w(x)=\frac12(K_a^{-1/2})_{xx}=\frac1\pi\int_0^\infty R_{xx}d\nu$ and $\Sigma(x,y)=\frac2\pi\int_0^\infty R_{xy}^2d\nu$, with $\Gamma(x)$ and $G_a(x,y)$ the analogues of $G_0$, $w_0$ and the static correlations.

Line: $\Gamma=1/\kappa_a+d/\kappa_h$, $w=\ln d/(2\pi\sqrt{\kappa_h})+O(1)$, $\Sigma=2\ln2\,d/(\pi\kappa_h^{3/2})(1+o(1))$; cubic ($L\to\infty$, $d\to\infty$): $\Gamma\to1/\kappa_a+2\gamma_3/\kappa_h$, $G_a\to c_\phi+g_\infty(x-y)$, while $w,\Sigma$ tend to the unanchored values with $O(d^{-3})$.
Mutual cost of two held sources $\mathcal E_{12}=-g_1g_2G_a(x_1,x_2)$, exact for every $L$ on both graphs; constant if one source is at the anchor.

Cubic torus, $L\to\infty$ first: image form $\mathcal E_{12}=-g_1g_2c_\phi-\frac{g_1g_2}{4\pi\kappa_h}[|x_1-x_2|^{-1}-|x_1-h|^{-1}-|x_2-h|^{-1}]$; the unanchored $1/|\mathbf r|$ law holds for $|\mathbf r|/D_X\to0$; with one source fixed it falls as $|\mathbf r|^{-2}$ or faster; at fixed midpoint it is $+3g_1g_2/(4\pi\kappa_h|\mathbf r|)$.

On the ring the mutual cost is a quadratic polynomial in the distances, independent of the separation for $L\to\infty$ at fixed distance of the nearer source: no long-range mark in any order of the limits.

Exact cost $C(x)=\mu F_0+\frac1{2\pi}\int_0^\infty\ln(1+2\mu F_2R_{xx})d\nu-\frac{\mu^2F_1^2\Gamma}{2(1+2\mu F_2\Gamma)}$ and $g_s$-linear cost $W(x)=\mu F_1\phi_a(x)/(1+2\mu F_2\Gamma(x))$ of one held body with the anchor.

$C^{(1)}=\mu(F_0+F_2w)$, $C^{\rm mark}=-\frac{\mu^2}2(F_1^2\Gamma+F_2^2\Sigma)$, $W^{(1)}=\mu F_1\phi_a$, $W^{\rm mark}=-2\mu^2F_1F_2\Gamma\phi_a$; at leading order in the grip $W^{(1)}=2\hat bC^{(1)}\phi_a$ and $W^{\rm mark}=2\hat\beta C^{\rm mark}\phi_a$ at every place.

$\rho_{\rm mark}=\frac{4F_2(F_0+F_2\bar w)\bar\Gamma}{F_1^2\bar\Gamma+F_2^2\bar\Sigma}(1+a_{\rm mark})$, $a_{\rm mark}=\bar\phi_a\Delta\Gamma/(\bar\Gamma\Delta\phi_a)$, exact at order $s^2$, the same for every level and both branches; defined as $s$-coefficients for every member, and referring to the lowest eigenvector of the stated contract iff (5.10) holds at $s=1$ ((5.26) for a pair).

$\rho_{{\rm bond},i}=\frac{\bar G_{12}\Delta\Psi+\bar\Psi\Delta G_{12}}{\bar G_{12}+\hat\beta_1\hat\beta_2\bar\Sigma_{12}/4}\cdot\frac{1+\hat\beta_i\hat b_i\bar w(\bar x)}{2\hat b_i\Delta\phi_a(\bar x)}$, $\Psi=\hat\beta_1\phi_a(x_1)+\hat\beta_2\phi_a(x_2)$, exact at order $\mu_1\mu_2$, the same for every level and both branches.

In the controlled regime $F_0^{(i)}\ne0$, $\varepsilon^2=\max_i(|F_2^{(i)}|\bar w/|F_0^{(i)}|,\hat\beta_i^2\bar\Sigma/\bar\Gamma,|\hat\beta_1\hat\beta_2|\bar\Sigma_{12}/\bar G_{12})\ll1$: $\rho_{\rm mark}=(\hat\beta/\hat b)(1+a_{\rm mark})(1+O(\varepsilon^2))$ and $\rho_{{\rm bond},i}$ = (midpoint term plus anchor term)$(1+O(\varepsilon^2))$; for $\Delta\Gamma=\Delta G_{12}=0$ the conditions of (2.18) with $G_0\to\Gamma$; grips with $F_0=0$ give both ratios $O(\eta_0^2)$ in their weak-grip regime (no weighing).

Exactly, $a_{\rm mark}=\frac{2\bar\phi_a}{g_s\bar\Gamma}\frac{\Delta g_h}{\Delta g_s-\Delta g_h}$ and $a_{\rm bond}=\frac{\bar\phi_1+\bar\phi_2}{2g_s\bar G_{12}}\frac{\Delta g_h(x_1)+\Delta g_h(x_2)}{\Delta g_s(\bar x)-\Delta g_h(\bar x)}$; on the cubic torus ($L\to\infty$) $a\to0$ iff the image difference is small against the direct one, so distance from the anchor alone does not suffice; at the mirror placement ($\Delta g_s=0$) $a_{\rm mark}\to2[c_\phi+g_\infty((1,R,0))]/\Gamma_\infty$ at every $d$.

Cubic torus, $L\to\infty$ first, non-cancellation $|\delta\cdot\hat e_s|\ge c|\delta|$ at the center of the comparison, $1\ll R$, $|\delta|\ll R\ll d$: $a_{\rm mark}=-\frac{2c_\phi}{\Gamma_\infty}\frac{R^2}{d^2}\frac{\delta\cdot\hat e_h}{\delta\cdot\hat e_s}+O(R^2\eta/(cd^2))$, $\eta=R^{-1}+(|\delta|^2+1)/(cR^2)+R^2/(cd^2)$.

Cubic torus, $L\to\infty$, then $d\to\infty$ at fixed relative placement with $\Delta g_s\ne0$, or under non-cancellation with $R/d\to0$ at fixed $c$: $a_{\rm bond}=O(R^2/(cd^2))\to0$, and in the controlled regime $\rho_{\rm mark}=1$, $\rho_{{\rm bond},i}=m_{\mathbf r}$ for every level and both branches, at order $\mu^2$ and leading order in the grip, iff the grips are square with a common $\hat\beta$; in the lowest eigenvector of the stated contract iff also (5.10) for one body and (5.26) for the pair at $\alpha_i=-2M_{k_i}|F_2^{(i)}|$; at leading order no grip gives $\rho_{\rm mark}=1$ at every comparison.

Line ($L\to\infty$ first), every comparison with $\Delta m\ne0$: $a_{\rm mark}=\frac{(\kappa_h/\kappa_a+\bar m)\Delta d}{(\kappa_h/\kappa_a+\bar d)\Delta m}$, $m_x=\min(d_x,d_s)$ on the source side and 0 across; equal to 1 between anchor and source, $>1$ straddling the source, of the sign of $d_x-d_{x'}$ across the anchor; at leading order in $\varepsilon$ no grip gives $\rho_{\rm mark}=1$ at every comparison.

Line ($L\to\infty$ first), comparisons with both placements (both bodies of a pair) between anchor and source: $a_{\rm mark}=1$; square grips give $\rho_{\rm mark}=2$; $\rho_{\rm mark}=1$ iff $8F_0F_2=F_1^2$, and then $\rho_{{\rm bond},i}=1+s/(4(\kappa_h/\kappa_a+\bar d_{\rm near}))$, equal to $m_{\mathbf r}=1$ only for $d_{\rm near}/s\to\infty$; linear grip: $\rho=0$.

open_issues: The ratios use differences between placements with means of the place-dependent costs; the anchor terms come from that extension while the place-wise relation of Step 6 holds at every place; which notion of weighing the programme adopts with an anchor is open.
Finite-L corrections to the image form (5.15) are not derived in closed form; only L to infinity first is treated.
The unanchored constants w and Σ of the infinite cubic lattice are not evaluated, and the O(1), o(1) terms of (5.13) on the line are not derived.
Out of scope: formation of the mark with an anchor, moving bodies and inertia, cells with finitely many places, other anchors, typicality.
